text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.69% today to $131.62, extending a steep four-day slide that saw the stock drop nearly $9 from its peak on September 15th. The immediate trigger was a drop in crude prices: after a pipeline attack spooked markets, Saudi Arabia announced it would release additional crude supplies to offset any disruption, sending oil prices lower and easing the supply-shock premium that had driven prices up earlier in the week. With US oil trading around $107 per barrel today versus highs of $141+ earlier this week, the reversal in oil prices directly pressured the stock.

The broader backdrop for oil and energy stocks has also shifted toward easing geopolitical tension. Reports that the Trump administration believes the Iran conflict may be winding down, and signals that Tehran is open to a deal, have reduced the fear premium that was pushing crude higher. While new US leverage over China and India via tariffs on Russian oil could support prices longer-term, today's immediate narrative—more Saudi supply, less acute geopolitical risk—favors lower oil prices in the near term.
